recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No further FHIR-core source work is needed for FHIR-17226 unless a future work group decision changes whether POST search URL parameters must be supported.
issue_request: FHIR-17226 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-core STU3 issue asking the RESTful search specification to define what happens when an HTTP POST search supplies search parameters in both the URL query string and the application/x-www-form-urlencoded body. The accepted resolution said parameters may appear in either place with the same meaning, and using both places is equivalent to repeating parameters.
initial_application: The issue was applied in git-svn commit 0f3fd3eddea935b3926919a698d6f90a1ca1e49f, matching Jira's svn revision 13947 comment. That commit added HTTP-page prose saying POST search parameters may appear in both the URL and body, have the same meaning in either place, and are equivalent to repeated parameters. Later R5 search/http work moved and reshaped this content; commit e441170220c19e992f803667b245e63dcdd508cf moved transport-protocol content from source/search.html to source/http.html, and the combined branch's FHIR-31944 reconciliation commit 147114dc2a42836ae64f0d31a75bbf998a094e2e restores the explicit accepted-parameter equivalence rule.
additional_context: The active build navigation lists source/http.html as the RESTful API page with source/search.html beneath it. Current source/http.html says servers SHALL support POST body search parameters, MAY support query parameters on POST, and, when a server accepts a search parameter in the URL of a POST search, there is no semantic difference from supplying it in the body; accepted URL and body parameters SHALL be combined into a single set, with repeats treated as repeats. Current source/search.html also requires self links to disclose the parameters actually used. FHIR-31944 is a later Published issue in the same POST-search family and is already represented on the combined branch.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit because the current active FHIR-core source already states the FHIR-17226 rule in the necessary location, with later FHIR-31944 context explaining optional support and self-link behavior for POST URL parameters.

related_jiras.note: Later Published POST search clarity issue that completed the current source wording for POST body parameters, optional URL parameters, URL/body equivalence, restrictions, and self links; already represented on the combined branch.
Later Published search-page restructuring issue moved search transport-protocol guidance from source/search.html to source/http.html, affecting where the FHIR-17226 rule now lives.
